title: Use coercivity and a squeezed trial to price exact-sector conditioning
statement: The sectorwise coercivity controls the full exact critical grand trace. A paid sublinear-energy trial rules out r>1 normalization; the vacuum denominator then bounds every K,K count by binom(K+2,2)^2 exp[beta-beta sqrt(K/6)] at every normalizable fugacity. Adaptive fugacity and positive mixtures do not remove this conditioning cost.

assumptions: Actual root review accepts the all-occupation analytic obstructions at its stated scope, without a final snapshot hash pin. This is high occupation on THREE sites, not fixed-density bulk complexity. Fixed-L positive transfer tails differ from the exact Gibbs tails; necessary mesh growth is not sufficient convergence or a continuous-time runtime lower bound. Direct fixed-mode canonical diagonalization is polynomial in K; non-Gibbs umbrellas/importance and number-squeezed/Bogoliubov descriptions remain live.
